summary: A discrepancy between the economic value of a sufficient asset's minimum balance and the native currency's existential deposit allows users to pay transaction fees at a fraction of their intended cost, enabling potential DoS via fee evasion.
details: Fee conversion uses the ratio between a sufficient asset's minimum balance and the native existential deposit. However, the economic value of these two figures can be entirely unrelated. An attacker choosing to pay fees in an asset whose minimum balance has a much lower market value than the native existential deposit can pay only a tiny fraction of the intended fee. This effectively allows DoS by enabling spam transactions at negligible cost, and may also allow censoring of legitimate transactions paid in the native currency.

database_specific.title: Discrepancy between economic value of minimum asset balance may allow evading fee payment
